title: Crypto holds rebound as ETF inflows rise; portfolio reaches $146,325
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded around $85,950, up 1.2% over 24 hours, while ether was near $2,742, up 0.8%. The broader rebound extended beyond the two largest coins: the CoinDesk 20 index gained 2.2%, with several major memecoins among the strongest performers. Bitcoin had pulled back from its move above $87,000, so the market was holding gains without extending them uniformly.

The macro backdrop was more supportive. WTI crude fell more than 2% to below $90 a barrel, alongside stronger equities. Cheaper oil could reduce inflation pressure, although it does not establish a change in Federal Reserve policy. Short covering also accompanied the crypto rebound. That combination helps explain the move, but does not establish a single cause or guarantee continuing demand.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs attracted about $999 million in net inflows, their strongest session since October 2025. Ether ETFs added roughly $270 million. BlackRock's bitcoin fund led with $381 million, followed by Ark and Fidelity. These flows provide concrete evidence of demand through regulated investment products, even as liquidation activity makes the price rally harder to interpret on its own.

Circle disclosed that Binance bought $100 million of its shares and agreed to an expanded five-year USDC partnership. The transaction closed on September 17. Circle will pay monthly incentives linked to USDC held through its wallet infrastructure, while Binance promotes the stablecoin. This gives Binance both an ownership interest and a commercial incentive to expand USDC distribution, tightening the relationship between an issuer and a major exchange.

Animoca Brands and Currenc Group suspended discussions on their proposed reverse merger. Both companies said the expected closing timetable no longer suited their near-term and medium-term goals. Animoca still intends to seek a major exchange listing and is progressing its audited accounts. The suspension delays a planned public-market route for a large Web3 investor; it does not provide a replacement timetable.

Our portfolio stands at about $146,325: $13,590 in the active treasury and $132,735 in the cold-storage Safe. That is $2,336 higher, or 1.62%, than the previous comparable snapshot. The Safe's 26.74 million directly held ARC tokens are unchanged in quantity and worth about $112,282, accounting for roughly 77% of net portfolio value before additional ARC exposure in liquidity pools.

The two Aerodrome WETH/ARC pools total about $17,642. Active-treasury Aerodrome value rose by $198 to $978 at the protocol level. Other exposures include roughly $4,947 of cbETH, $1,579 of tokenized equities and $592 on Hyperliquid. Aave shows about $9,353 supplied against $2,921 of USDC debt, with health factors of 3.40 and 2.27. Fluid is only about $199 net, but its $1,005 debt and 1.08 health factor leave little liquidation headroom. ARC concentration remains the largest portfolio risk.
